title: Water, sewer and grease (ACSA), well and septic, propane and natural gas, stormwater and land disturbance, and DEQ air rules for a glass studio
question: What utility and environmental approvals does a glass studio in Albemarle County need: public water and sewer connection and the grease program, or well and septic; propane or natural gas supply for the furnace; stormwater and land disturbance permits for site work; and whether the gas-fired furnace and kilns need a Virginia DEQ air permit?
office: Albemarle County Service Authority (public water and sewer, connection charges, backflow and FOG programs); Blue Ridge Health District Environmental Health (private wells and septic); Community Development Engineering (Virginia Erosion and Stormwater Management Program, land disturbance permits); Albemarle County Fire Rescue (LP-gas permit) and Community Development Building Inspections (gas piping and tank permits); Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (air permits)
summary: Utilities and environment are the last layer of a studio's approvals. Inside the Albemarle County Service Authority's jurisdictional area, ACSA supplies water and sewer, charges system development and Rivanna capacity charges by meter size for new connections, requires a signed building permit before it schedules a meter, expects its General Water and Sewer Conditions and water and sewer data sheets on site plans, enforces backflow prevention, and requires food service to install a grease (FOG) collection device and get a FOG permit. Outside that area the Blue Ridge Health District permits private wells and septic systems (well permit $350, sewage construction permit from $525 in Albemarle on its 2019 schedule) and a cafe's wastewater must fit the septic design. Furnace fuel is natural gas from the utility where a main exists, or propane: a propane tank needs a mechanical permit (above-ground tank $120, gas lines $40) and the Fire Marshal's LP-gas permit, and the County collects a consumer utility tax on commercial gas and electric bills. Site work disturbing more than 10,000 square feet (or any land disturbance in the County's erosion and stormwater program) needs Community Development's plan review and land disturbance permit ($235 plus 4% under an acre, $2,205 plus 4% from one to five acres) and a certified Responsible Land Disturber. A gas-fired glass furnace or kiln is exempt from DEQ's minor new source review permit as fuel-burning equipment under 50,000,000 Btu per hour, and a small studio's total uncontrolled emissions fall far below the exemption table, so no air permit is expected, but keep burner ratings and fuel records and ask DEQ's regional office if you add many burners or use lead or other listed pollutants.

legal_basis.quote: A person shall not conduct any land-disturbing activity until (i) he has submitted to the appropriate VESMP authority an application that includes a permit registration statement, if required, a soil erosion control and stormwater management plan or an executed agreement in lieu of a plan, if required, and (ii) the VESMP authority has issued its land-disturbance approval.

In addition, as a prerequisite to engaging in an approved land-disturbing activity, the name of the individual who will be assisting the owner in carrying out the activity and holds a Responsible Land Disturber certificate pursuant to § 62.1-44.15:30 shall be submitted to the VESMP authority.

The Board, after having studied air pollution in the various areas of the Commonwealth, its causes, prevention, control and abatement, shall have the power to promulgate regulations, including emergency regulations, abating, controlling and prohibiting air pollution throughout or in any part of the Commonwealth in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Process Act (§ 2.2-4000 et seq.)

Except as provided in subsection C of this section, the provisions of this article apply to (i) the construction of any new stationary source or any project (which includes any addition or replacement of an emissions unit, any modification to an emissions unit or any combination of these changes), and (ii) the reduction of any stack outlet elevation at any stationary source.
Fuel burning equipment units (external combustion units, not engines and turbines) and space heaters in a single application as follows:
(4) Using gaseous fuel with a maximum heat input of less than 50,000,000 Btu per hour.
(3) Using liquid and gaseous fuel with a maximum heat input of less than 10,000,000 Btu per hour.
New stationary sources with uncontrolled emission rates less than all of the emission rates specified in the table in this subdivision shall be exempt from the provisions of this article.
Permits shall not be issued to newly constructed or extensively remodeled food establishments until a certificate of occupancy has been issued by the Building Official.

steps.step: Find out whether the parcel has public water and sewer (ACSA jurisdictional area) or is on well and septic
steps.who: You; Albemarle County Service Authority customer service; Community Development GIS
steps.how: ACSA serves the County's Development Areas and some other parcels inside its jurisdictional area; the County GIS shows the jurisdictional area boundary and the pre-application meeting invites ACSA when water and sewer matter. A hot shop uses little process water (slurry sinks, cold-working coolant, wash-up) but a cafe needs potable water and sewer capacity. Changing the jurisdictional area for a parcel is a Board of Supervisors action (the County fee schedule has an 'ACSJA - Amend Service Authority Jurisdictional Area' line) and takes months; plan on the service you have.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Pre-Application Meeting page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026); Planning & Site Development page (Service Authority Jurisdictional Request)
steps.paraphrase: Planning, Zoning and Engineering staff attend the pre-application meeting, joined when relevant by VDOT, the Service Authority for water and sewer, and Fire Rescue.

steps.step: On public utilities: put ACSA's conditions and data sheets on the site plan, pay connection charges, and set up service
steps.who: Your engineer; Albemarle County Service Authority (engineering and customer service)
steps.how: ACSA's design and construction standards (General Water and Sewer Construction Specifications, Approved Products List, Rules & Regulations) govern any new water or sewer line; the current General Water and Sewer Conditions go on all site plans and construction plans, and the developer's engineer completes the Water Data Sheet and Sewer Data Sheet when site plans or construction plans are submitted. New connections pay ACSA system development charges and Rivanna Water and Sewer Authority capacity charges (by meter size; installation charges and the North Fork special rate district are extra; current amounts are on ACSA's Connection Charges page). To start service, give the service and mailing addresses and a daytime phone by phone, the Service Request page or in person; for a new connection all County inspections should be complete and ACSA needs at least a signed building permit before it schedules the meter; a $13 initial bill fee appears on the first bill. For an existing connection, coordinate the changeover date with the landlord or previous tenant.
steps.deadline: Data sheets with the site plan; meter after the building permit is signed
steps.fee: ACSA system development charge and RWSA capacity charge by meter size (see ACSA Connection Charges); $13 initial bill fee
steps.basis: Albemarle County Service Authority, New Construction Guidelines page (Internet Archive copy of 15 May 2026), Connection Charges page (Internet Archive copy of 10 April 2026) and Start or Stop Service page (Internet Archive copy of 15 May 2026)
steps.quote: Please note that a $13 initial bill fee will be charged to your account appearing on your first month's bill.

steps.step: Install backflow prevention and, for a cafe, a grease collection device with an ACSA FOG permit
steps.who: Your plumber; Albemarle County Service Authority compliance programs
steps.how: ACSA's Cross Connection and Backflow Prevention Program requires backflow preventers where the premises can contaminate the public supply (a commercial building with process sinks, boilers or irrigation will usually need a tested device; ACSA publishes a brochure, a list of certified testers and a test report form). Food service establishments must have a Fats, Oils and Grease collection system that is installed, inspected and maintained; use ACSA's New Restaurant Packet, FOG Permit Application Instructions and FOG Permit Application. Even on septic, keep grease out of the drains.
steps.deadline: Before the cafe opens; backflow devices tested as ACSA requires
steps.fee: Not stated on the pages read
steps.basis: Albemarle County Service Authority, Compliance Programs page (Internet Archive copy of 6 March 2026)
steps.quote: ACSA promotes and enforces backflow prevention to reduce health risks caused by cross-connections.

steps.step: On well and septic: get the Health District's well and sewage permits sized for the studio and any cafe
steps.who: You and an onsite soil evaluator or engineer; Blue Ridge Health District Environmental Health, Charlottesville/Albemarle office
steps.how: Outside the ACSA area, apply to the Environmental Health office at 1138 Rose Hill Drive for a private well construction permit and a sewage construction permit (or a certification letter for an existing system), with or without an Onsite Soil Evaluator or professional engineer's documentation; the County's building permit application then needs the VDH well and septic construction permits, a well log for parcels under 21 acres and a BTEX report in LUST or BTEX zones (see building_permit_residential). A cafe's wastewater flow must be within the system's design, and the Health District's food plan review will ask about the well and septic. The district's 2019 fee schedule lists an Albemarle well permit at $350 and a sewage construction permit at $525 (under 1,000 gallons a day, no OSE/PE documentation) or $325 with OSE/PE documentation, with combined and repair permits priced separately.
steps.deadline: Before the building permit is issued
steps.fee: Private well construction permit $350; sewage construction permit $525 (no OSE/PE documentation) or $325 (with documentation) under 1,000 gallons a day; combined sewage and well permit $875 or $675 (Albemarle column of the district's 2019 fee schedule)
steps.basis: Blue Ridge Health District, Environmental Health page (live); District Environmental Health Fee Schedule effective July 1, 2019; Albemarle County Community Development, Application Requirements page
steps.quote: Private Well Construction & Abandondment Permit with or without OSE/PE Documentation

steps.step: Arrange furnace fuel: natural gas service or a propane tank, with the County and Fire Marshal permits
steps.who: You; Columbia Gas of Virginia (where a main exists) or a propane supplier; Community Development Building Inspections; Fire Rescue
steps.how: Ask the gas utility whether a main serves the parcel and what load it can supply; a new commercial service and meter come from the utility. Otherwise plan a propane tank: the tank and piping need the County mechanical permits (above-ground tanks $120; gas or oil lines $40; the furnace line $75 may also apply), the tank location must satisfy the site plan, setbacks and any Entrance Corridor screening, and storage and use of LP-gas at a business of any size needs the Fire Marshal's LP-gas operational permit ($200 a year per location, with inspection). Oxygen for torches is a compressed gas permit (see glass_studio_fire_permits). Electric service for kilns and annealers is an electrical sub-permit and may need a service change ($35).
steps.deadline: Before fuel is delivered or the furnace is fired
steps.fee: Mechanical above-ground tank $120; gas or oil lines $40; furnace $75; electrical service change $35 (plus 4%); Fire Marshal LP-gas permit $200 a year
steps.basis: Community Development fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 20 August 2026); 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2, LP-gas); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: The County's mechanical fee line for above-ground tanks.

steps.step: Expect the County's consumer utility tax on gas and electric bills
steps.who: You; the utilities (collected on the bill)
steps.how: The County levies consumer utility taxes collected by the utilities: commercial or industrial gas at $0.0638 per CCF for the first 4,500 CCF and $0.0110 per CCF above that on non-interruptible service ($0.0588 per CCF for the first 4,770 CCF on interruptible service); commercial electricity at $0.006161 per kWh for the first 48,693 kWh and $0.001636 above; industrial electricity at $0.005265 per kWh for the first 56,980 kWh and $0.000934 above. Propane delivered by truck is not on the County's utility tax table.
steps.fee: Per the County's consumer utility tax table
steps.basis: Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Tax Rates page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026)
steps.paraphrase: Commercial gas is taxed at one rate per CCF up to 4,500 CCF a month and a lower rate above that.

steps.step: For site work: land disturbance (VESMP) plan review and permit from Community Development Engineering
steps.who: Your engineer and a certified Responsible Land Disturber; Community Development Engineering
steps.how: Building a new studio, parking or a tank pad disturbs land. Projects disturbing more than 10,000 square feet need the County's engineering review (the Engineering checklists in the Forms Library) and a land disturbance permit under the Virginia Erosion and Stormwater Management Program; state law forbids starting until the VESMP authority issues its land-disturbance approval, and the owner must name a certificate-holding Responsible Land Disturber. Fees on the County schedule: small construction activity under 10,000 square feet in a common plan of development or 10,000 square feet to under one acre, $235 plus 4% for plan review and permit; one to five acres, $2,205 plus 4%; five to ten acres, $2,775 plus 4%; VESMP-exempt small disturbances (no water quantity or quality criteria) under one acre or one to five acres carry their own lines (the latter $565 plus 4%). Stormwater management facilities shown at the pre-application stage become part of the site plan; the County also charges annual maintenance and bond fees.
steps.fee: VESMP small construction activity 10,000 sq. ft. to under 1 acre: $235 plus 4%; 1 to under 5 acres: $2,205 plus 4%; 5 to under 10 acres: $2,775 plus 4%; VESMP-exempt 1 to 5 acres: $565 plus 4%
steps.basis: Va. Code § 62.1-44.15:34(A); Albemarle County Community Development, Application Requirements page (Internet Archive copy of 13 August 2026); Community Development fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 20 August 2026); County Code Chapter 17 (Water Protection Ordinance; Municode, not reprinted)
steps.paraphrase: Check the land disturbance rules before you file the building permit application.

steps.step: Check the DEQ air permit exemption for the furnace, glory hole and kilns, and keep the records
steps.who: You and your mechanical contractor; Virginia DEQ regional office if in doubt
steps.how: Virginia's minor new source review permit applies to new stationary sources, but fuel-burning equipment is exempt unit by unit when it burns gaseous fuel at under 50,000,000 Btu per hour, liquid or mixed fuel under 10,000,000 Btu per hour, or solid fuel under 1,000,000 Btu per hour; a studio furnace, glory hole and gas kilns are far below those ratings. A new source is also exempt when its total uncontrolled emissions stay below the table in 9VAC5-80-1105(C) (for example 100 tons a year of carbon monoxide, 40 of nitrogen oxides, 25 of particulate matter, 0.6 of lead); exempt fuel-burning units are not counted in that sum. Keep each unit's manufacturer heat-input rating, your fuel purchase records and the batch materials list (lead crystal, cadmium or other metal colorants are the pollutants most likely to matter) so you can show the exemption. If you add many burners, a large bulk tank, or melt leaded or metal-colored batch at scale, ask DEQ's regional air permitting staff before installing; deq.virginia.gov refuses automated readers, so no DEQ page is cited here.
steps.deadline: Before construction of any unit that would not be exempt
steps.quote: Facilities exempted by subsection B of this section shall not be included in the summation of uncontrolled emissions for purposes of exempting new stationary sources under this subsection.

steps.step: Plan waste handling: cullet, kiln wash, abrasives and coolant
steps.who: You; your waste hauler; ACSA or the Health District for drains
steps.how: Broken and scrap glass (cullet) is ordinary solid waste or recyclable; grinding and polishing slurry from cold-working should settle out before anything reaches a drain (ACSA sewer rules and septic health both forbid dumping solids), and used coolant, kiln wash and any lead-bearing batch or dust need a waste determination under DEQ's hazardous waste rules if they carry regulated metals. None of this needs a County permit of its own; it shows up in the Certified Engineer's Report for the Zoning Clearance (performance standards for industrial uses) and in ACSA's or the Health District's review of the plumbing.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Zoning Clearance page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026) (Certified Engineer's Report); ACSA Rules & Regulations (PDF, not read)
steps.paraphrase: A Zoning Clearance can depend on the County accepting a Certified Engineer's Report.

escalation.next: Appeal of the County Engineer's determination (the Community Development fee schedule has an 'Appeal – County Engineer Determination' line), then the Board of Supervisors under the Water Protection Ordinance (County Code Chapter 17, Municode)

escalation.next: Request for an informal review by the district, then appeal to the State Sewage Handling and Disposal Appeal Review Board (the district's fee schedule lists an appeal fee of $135, not collected locally)

caveats: serviceauthority.org and www.albemarle.org refuse automated readers; the ACSA and County pages cited are Internet Archive copies (dates in the sources). County quotes carry paraphrases because the County's terms bar reposting. ACSA's connection charge amounts are in a table that was not read cleanly; the live Connection Charges page has them.

deq.virginia.gov refuses automated readers and its newest Internet Archive copies are from 2023, so the air permit analysis rests on 9VAC5-80-1100 and 9VAC5-80-1105 (read live). The statement that a glass studio's emissions fall below the exemption table is an inference from the equipment's size, not a DEQ determination; ask DEQ's regional office if the studio uses leaded or metal-colored batch at scale.

The County's Water Protection Ordinance (County Code Chapter 17) and its land disturbance thresholds were not read (Municode); the 10,000 square foot trigger comes from the County's Application Requirements page and the fee schedule's VESMP lines. Whether a studio in an existing building with no site work needs any engineering approval is a Community Development question.
The Health District's fee schedule is dated July 1, 2019 and may have changed; the well and septic amounts are the Albemarle column.

Natural gas availability depends on the parcel; the Columbia Gas home page was read live but says nothing about Albemarle service areas. Dominion Energy's Virginia page was read for electric service only.

Not confirmed by lexflow's software: the words once quoted for the legal basis '9VAC5-80-1100(C)' (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title9/agency5/chapter80/section1100/) were not found on the cited page as lexflow read it (not found word for word in the cited page as read on 20 October 2026). Those claims now rest on the cited page as read, without a matched quote; check them at the link before relying on them.
